docs.title: Crash
docs.text:
Crash is a real-time multiplayer crash game played with demo coins. Every round is provably fair, and you can check any round in your browser.

Formerly BTCGambler.

Play Crash

Demo coins only

Crash uses demo coins. They have no real value. There is no way to pay in money or cash out.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Play in one click. Continue as a guest, or log in with a 4zam account (Google, Microsoft or GitHub).
  • Live rounds. A multiplier climbs from 1.00x until it crashes. Pull out before the crash to win.
  • Provably fair. Each round is seeded from a published hash chain and a future Bitcoin block. A built-in verifier recomputes the crash point.
  • Two demo currencies. Fake Points (FAKE) and demo Bitcoin (BTC) on a private test network.
  • Live chat and a full bet history.

docs.text:

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Crash runs as one Docker Compose stack behind a host reverse proxy. The server is the authority for every round: the browser only sends bets and cash-outs.

docs.title: Stack
docs.text: Part Technology Frontend React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind and shadcn/ui Backend Django 5.2 on Python 3.12 with Django REST Framework Realtime Django Channels on daphne, with a Redis channel layer (WebSockets) Background jobs Celery worker and Celery beat Data PostgreSQL 16 and Redis 7 (Redis holds no durable state) Chain Bitcoin Core in regtest mode, reachable only inside the stack Sign-in 4zam (OpenID Connect) and one-click guests Web Caddy serves the app and proxies the API and WebSockets. A host Caddy handles TLS.

docs.title: Services
docs.text:
• web: serves the built frontend and forwards /api and /ws to the backend.
  • backend: the Django API and WebSocket server (game updates, live bets and chat).
  • game-engine: a single process that runs the rounds: betting window, multiplier, crash and settlement.
  • worker and beat: Celery jobs for faucet payouts, withdrawals, deposit credits, block mining on the test network and guest cleanup.
  • fairness-sealer: checks every 5 minutes for a committed chain whose salt block has 6 confirmations, and records the block hash once two block explorers agree on it.
  • postgres: players, bets, rounds, the fairness chain and the money ledger.
  • redis: the WebSocket channel layer and the Celery broker.
  • bitcoind: the regtest Bitcoin node used by the faucet and withdrawals.
  • migrate and wallet setup: one-shot jobs that run database migrations and prepare the node wallet on deploy.

docs.title: Money
docs.text:
• Every balance change is an entry in a ledger in PostgreSQL. Bets settle there instantly.
  • Only the faucet and withdrawals touch the regtest chain. Withdrawals are queued and sent by a background job.
  • Nothing in the stack has real value: FAKE is a play currency and BTC lives on a private regtest network.

docs.title: Rounds and fairness
docs.text:
• The engine only runs rounds while at least one player is connected.
  • Each round's seed comes from a pre-published SHA-256 hash chain, salted with the hash of a future Bitcoin block. See Provably fair.
  • If no sealed chain covers the next round, the engine pauses instead of falling back to a house-picked seed.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
• CI runs on every pull request and every push to main: a secret scan, backend tests, frontend lint, tests and build, deploy script checks and an end-to-end smoke test of the full production stack (deploy, play a round, back up, restore and roll back).
  • Deploys: a staging stack deploys on every push to the staging branch. Production deploys are started by hand.
  • Backups of the database and the node wallet run daily, and a restore drill runs weekly.

docs.title: Signing in
docs.text:
There are two ways in:

  • Continue as Guest. One click creates a guest player with a generated name (for example player-ab23cd45ef) and 1,000 FAKE. There is no password.
  • Log in. This opens the 4zam sign-in page, where you choose Google, Microsoft or GitHub. A 4zam account keeps your balance across devices.

Good to know:

  • A guest session lasts 7 days and renews while you play.
  • Logging out leaves the guest and its balance behind. There is no way back into it. A guest that stays idle for 7 days is removed.
  • If you log in while playing as a guest, the guest becomes your 4zam account and keeps its balance. If that 4zam account has already played Crash, the guest balance is not merged into it.
  • Passwords and two-factor sign-in are managed in your 4zam account, not in Crash.

docs.title: How a round works
docs.text:
1. Betting opens for 15 seconds. Enter an amount and press Place Bet. You can also set an auto cash-out multiplier (1.01x or higher).
  2. The round starts at 1.00x and the multiplier climbs. It reaches 2x after about 12 seconds and 10x after about 38 seconds.
  3. Pull out before the crash. Press Pull Out or the Space key. Your bet is paid at the multiplier when the server received your cash-out.
  4. The round crashes at a point fixed before betting opened. Bets still riding lose.

Rules:

  • One bet per round. The largest bet is 1,000,000.
  • Once placed, a bet is locked in. Pull Out becomes available when the round starts.
  • Auto cash-out is sent from your browser tab, so keep the tab open and in front.
  • Crash points are capped at 50x. About 1 round in 33 crashes instantly at 1.00x, which gives the house an edge of about 3%.
  • Rounds only run while at least one player has Crash open. When nobody is connected, the game idles and starts again as soon as the next player arrives.
  • If no round can start (for example while a new fairness chain is being sealed), the chart shows "Rounds are paused".

On the game page you also get:

  • Active Bets: everyone's bet on the current round, its status and the result.
  • History: the last 5 crash points, colored by how high each round went.
  • Game chat: live chat for every player, guests included. Messages are up to 280 characters.

docs.title: Demo coins
docs.text:
Crash has two demo currencies. Neither has real value.

Currency What it is Shown with Fake Points (FAKE) Play balance. Guests start with 1,000 FAKE. 2 decimals Bitcoin (BTC) Demo Bitcoin on a private regtest network 8 decimals
  • The header shows your balance with a "demo coins" label at all times.
  • Pick the currency in the header dropdown. Your bets use that currency.
  • Bets settle instantly on the site's own ledger. Only the faucet and withdrawals use the Bitcoin test network.

docs.title: Wallet
docs.text:
The Wallets page shows each balance and its transaction history.

  • Faucet. Claim 0.5 demo BTC once every 24 hours. The faucet is off while you hold 5 demo BTC or more, and it has daily limits per IP address and for the whole site.
  • Withdrawals. Send demo BTC to an address on the test network. A small network fee is added on top. A withdrawal confirms in about a minute and cannot be undone. There is a daily limit of 10 demo BTC.
  • Transactions. Bets, payouts, faucet claims, deposits and withdrawals all appear in the history. Incoming transfers show while they confirm.

docs.title: Provably fair
docs.text:
Each crash point is fixed before betting opens. Crash uses a hash chain based on the Bustabit scheme:

  • The chain. The house generates a chain of 1,000,000 seeds where each seed is the SHA-256 hash of the next one. It publishes the last hash (the terminal hash) first.
  • The salt. At the same time it names a future Bitcoin block. Once that block is mined and has 6 confirmations, its hash becomes the client seed for every round in the chain. If the chain was published before that block was mined, the house could not know the hash when it committed to the chain.
  • Each round. The round's seed hash is shown before betting opens. After the crash, the seed is revealed. It hashes to the published seed hash, and that hash is the previous round's seed, all the way back to the terminal hash.
  • The crash point comes from HMAC-SHA256 of the seed with the client seed and the round number (the nonce).

Rounds from before the hash chain used an older rule where the house picked both seeds. The page says so.

The Provably Fair page lists the published chain (terminal hash, commit time, salt block and its hash) and every round with its seeds. You can search by seed hash.

docs.title: Verify a round
docs.text:
Press Verify on any round in the Provably Fair page. The checks run in your browser:

  • It recomputes the crash point and checks it matches the one shown.
  • It checks that the revealed seed hashes to the seed hash published before the round.
  • It shows the chain and the salt block, with a link to look the block up on mempool.space.
  • Check the link to the commitment hashes the seed back to the chain's terminal hash.
  • Show the working lists each step of the calculation.

Trust limit

The house generates the chain. Once the salt block is mined, it knows the coming crash points, though it cannot change them. The chain is only fair if it was published before that block was mined. The commit time shown is the site's own record, not an independent timestamp. Crash states this on the Provably Fair page.

docs.title: Bets
docs.text:
• All Bets lists every bet on the site: player, amount, multiplier, net winnings, time and seed hash. Search by username and sort by any column except seed hash.
  • My Bets shows only your bets.
  • The seed hash links to that round on the Provably Fair page, where you can verify it.

docs.title: Profile and settings
docs.text:
• Profile: your username and the color of your name in chat.
  • Settings: dark mode on or off (dark is the default) and the animated background on or off.
  • If your device asks for reduced motion, the animated background stays off.

docs.title: On phones
docs.text: The game page stacks into one column on small screens. The chart, bet controls, active bets and chat all stay available.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Source code

The Crash source code is private. These steps are for people with access to the repository. To see the game, play it live.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Docker with Docker Compose 2.24 or newer
  • Python 3, curl, flock and ss (used by the deploy script)
  • Node.js 20.19 or newer, for frontend development and frontend tests

You do not need a Bitcoin node or a Redis server: the stack runs its own.

docs.title: Run the whole stack locally
docs.text:
The production Compose file runs locally as the local stack. It uses plain HTTP, generates throwaway secrets and allows guest sign-in only.

git rev-parse HEAD > REVISION
bash deploy/deploy.sh --stack local

Then open http://crash.localhost:18099.

Rounds pause until a chain is sealed

The game only runs rounds covered by a sealed fairness chain. A fresh local stack shows "Rounds are paused" until one is set up. Sealing a chain needs internet access to public Bitcoin block explorers and a future Bitcoin block with 6 confirmations, so expect about 2 to 3 hours from commit to the first round. The repository's fairness seeding runbook has the steps.

docs.title: Frontend only
docs.text:
To work on the frontend against a backend that is already running:

cd frontend
npm ci
npm run dev

The dev server runs on http://localhost:5173 and proxies /api and /ws to a backend at http://localhost:8000. Set VITE_DEV_BACKEND to use a backend somewhere else.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• Backend: pytest in backend/, against a PostgreSQL and a Redis.
  • Frontend: npm run lint, npm run test:unit and npm run build in frontend/.
  • Deploy package: the scripts in deploy/tests/, including a full smoke test of the production stack.
